blocking_focus: Complete the candidate-bound Tester MCP state matrix.

preservation_constraints.requirement: Keep frozen technical baseline `native_godot_project` passing. Do not treat this as a mandate to preserve the same visible asset, map, HUD family, or material choice if a higher-quality replacement is available and the PRD still fits.

Keep frozen technical baseline `host_godot_boot` passing. Do not treat this as a mandate to preserve the same visible asset, map, HUD family, or material choice if a higher-quality replacement is available and the PRD still fits.

task_specification.objective: Replace text-stacked upgrade choices with the required authored decision hierarchy while restoring spatially coherent authored-cemetery traversal and landmark visibility, and make the native dense-run performance contract deterministic and directly retestable without changing ordinary combat semantics.

diagnosis.root_cause: The arena defect is an integration mismatch between the authored cemetery package, gameplay collision/anchors, and shipped-camera occlusion handling; prior evidence lacks a traversal proof. Dense qualification is blocked by missing native-renderer-bound evidence, so the candidate needs a deterministic qualification bridge and bounded density safeguards while the host supplies the renderer verdict.

stop_conditions: Do not replace, split, hide, extract, duplicate, or reposition the preserved authored cemetery package.
Do not treat unavailable native-renderer collection as a candidate pass; carry final qualification to Host Runtime and Tester.
Do not expand into deferred automatic-attack audio or unrelated backlog gaps.

strategy.rationale: Use explicit player-facing choice replacement plus a materially different spatial root-cause strategy from camera transform tuning: restore authored-package bindings, collision and visibility isolation, and deterministic traversal anchors; separately harden dense qualification at its authoritative lifecycle boundary.

code: Run focused Godot script/resource syntax checks for all modified files and verify scene/resource references resolve.
Inspect collision layers/masks, navigation and spawn anchors, occluder bindings, upgrade-card icon/stat data, and editor/release guards for missing-resource or parse errors.
Confirm dense safeguards do not alter authoritative attack, damage, pooling, or run-state transitions when the probe is disabled.
runtime: Host Runtime recaptures native boot/integrity plus the arena matrix at spawn, critical route, cardinal landmark, near-contact/departure, and perimeter states, including ordinary movement/movement replay collision and visibility.

Host Runtime/Tester executes the dense prepare/advance/reset protocol at 1920x1080 for three reset-isolated cycles, compares baseline and dense metrics, and reruns release_convergence_dense_run_performance_contract on an eligible native renderer.

Tester exercises the replacement choice surface with keyboard, mouse, and gamepad focus, hover, pressed, unavailable, selected, pause/resume, and debounced commit behavior, then owns formal issue closure.
visual: Review shipped gameplay frames for cemetery scale, external depth, central landmark readability, aligned collision cues, stable occlusion behavior, and absence of proxy-floor or void artifacts.

Review the level-up draft for weapon or upgrade silhouettes, compact stat icons, truthful current-to-new deltas, restrained copy, and visible focus states while preserving the moonlit gothic visual language.

done_when: Text-stacked weapon and upgrade choices are replaced by three authored weapon or upgrade silhouettes, compact stat icons, restrained copy, and aligned current-to-new values.
Each choice shows no more than three decision-relevant stat deltas; unchanged, exhaustive, zero, NEW, and LOCKED rows are omitted, and NEW or LOCKED never appears in the CURRENT value column.
Keyboard, mouse, and gamepad focus, hover, pressed, unavailable, selected, and debounced-commit states are visibly distinct and remain correct across pause/resume.
The arena has expand/larger traversable scale with a coherent external world/external depth beyond the gameplay perimeter.
A central building/landmark remains visible during ordinary movement/movement replay; there is no disappearance or camera occlusion drift before approach, near contact, or after departure.
Prominent landmark geometry and the playable boundary/perimeter have aligned collision; the player and representative enemies cannot pass through the landmark or leave the authored play space.
Spawn, objective, navigation, and camera framing are anchored to native authored streets/terrain, with proxy/support clutter removed or minimized.
tasks.instructions: Replace text-stacked weapon and upgrade choices in the authored level-up surface with a concrete silhouette-led hierarchy: lead with recognizable weapon or upgrade silhouettes, add compact stat icons, show truthful current-to-new values for at most three decision-relevant deltas, omit unchanged/exhaustive rows, never place NEW or LOCKED in CURRENT, and implement complete keyboard, mouse, and gamepad focus/hover/pressed/unavailable/selected states with debounced commit across pause/resume. In the same bounded presentation/integration task, repair the preserved authored cemetery rather than retuning camera transforms in isolation: rebase player spawn, objective anchors, navigation, landmark collision, and camera visibility handling onto native streets/terrain; provide expand/larger traversable scale and external world/external depth; keep the central building/landmark readable through ordinary movement/movement replay; use bounded transparency/selective occluder handling instead of whole-landmark hiding; and verify collision agreement at the boundary/perimeter. Keep the authored environment as one intact runtime instance and remove or minimize unrelated proxy geometry.
tasks.title: Replace text-stacked choices and restore authored arena spatial integrity

done_when: A deterministic dense-run scenario reaches the configured target density and records bounded frame-time/FPS, renderer classification, active enemy/projectile/pickup/effect/light/voice counts, subsystem samples, high-water marks, lifecycle deltas, and runtime-error count.

The three-cycle prepare/advance/reset protocol records requested, resolved, reset-isolation, cycle identity, setup generation, and next-frame reset receipts with comparable baseline and dense checkpoints.
Profiling is editor/qualification-gated, disabled or stripped for release exports, allocation/logging churn is bounded, and no per-frame unbounded scene scans are introduced.
A density guard caps or schedules nonessential work before pathological growth while preserving automatic combat cadence, enemy motion, damage causality, pooled-entity resets, and readable HUD.
tasks.instructions: Harden the authoritative run/director dense-profile boundary so Host Runtime can recapture the native qualification contract without relying on an unavailable collector during development. Reuse the fixed native_renderer_three_cycle contract and add only the missing deterministic bridge or safeguards: stable high-density setup, fixed sampling cadence, subsystem counters, renderer/preflight receipts, reset isolation, and bounded token-bucket scheduling or caps for nonessential presentation work. Keep the probe opt-in and editor-only, preserve ordinary wave balance and combat state, and surface pending or rejected software-renderer status instead of fabricating qualification.
tasks.title: Harden deterministic native dense-run qualification
